slides.title: Say this instead
slides.body: Use genial, buenísimo, or qué rico depending on the situation.

slides.title: A real example
slides.body: ¿Te gustó la película? — Sí, estuvo genial.

slides.title: Quick tip
slides.body:
Food: está riquísimo.
A plan: suena genial.
A person: es muy buena persona.

options: I'll send you a voice note now
quiz.meaning: I'll send you a voice note now.
quiz.example: Escúchalo cuando puedas. — Listen when you can.

correction.mistake: Pronouncing Ibiza, Mallorca, and México like English words
correction.tip: Spanish place names keep Spanish vowel sounds.

items: I didn't understand the last part

quiz.meaning: What a shame / That's too bad.
quiz.example: No puedo ir. — Qué pena. — I can't go. — That's too bad.

correction.mistake: Using triste for every unfortunate situation
correction.correction: Use qué pena or lo siento when reacting to bad news
correction.tip: Triste describes sadness; qué pena reacts to a situation.

correction.correction: Actualmente means currently; actually is en realidad
correction.example: En realidad, no vivo aquí. — Actually, I don't live here.

quiz.meaning: I like them / I get a good vibe from them.
quiz.example: Tu hermana me cae muy bien.

correction.mistake: Saying es aburrido when you mean someone feels bored
correction.correction: Es aburrido = he is boring. Está aburrido = he is bored.
correction.example: Juan es divertido, pero hoy está aburrido.
correction.tip: Ser describes character; estar describes a current state.

quiz.example: ¿Te ayudo? — No, gracias. Solo estoy mirando.

correction.mistake: Saying no necesito ayuda to every shop assistant
correction.correction: Solo estoy mirando sounds softer and more natural
correction.example: Gracias, solo estoy mirando por ahora.
correction.tip: Add por ahora to mean for now.

correction.mistake: Translating I feel like as siento como
correction.example: Tengo ganas de viajar. — I feel like travelling.
correction.tip: For a noun: tengo ganas de pizza also works casually.

items: Do you feel like going out?

quiz.example: Hoy estoy un poco de bajón.

correction.mistake: Using estoy cansado for every low-energy mood
correction.correction: Use estoy de bajón for low mood and estoy agotado for exhaustion
correction.tip: Match the phrase to mood, stress, or physical fatigue.

correction.mistake: Using cállate with strangers as a casual be quiet
correction.correction: Cállate can sound harsh; try habla más bajo
correction.tip: Direct commands often sound stronger than English learners expect.

items: I think I explained myself badly

quiz.phrase: Tengo una reserva a nombre de Ana.
options: I have a booking under Ana
quiz.meaning: I have a reservation under Ana's name.
quiz.example: Tengo una reserva para dos noches.

correction.correction: Reserva is the safest choice across Spain and Latin America
correction.example: Quisiera hacer una reserva para mañana.
correction.tip: Reservación is common in some regions, but reserva travels better.

correction.mistake: Translating just in case word for word
correction.correction: Use por si acaso, or simply por si + clause
correction.example: Te mando la dirección por si te pierdes.
correction.tip: Por si acaso can stand alone; por si introduces a possibility.

quiz.meaning: That time or plan works for me.
quiz.example: ¿A las ocho? — Sí, me viene bien.

correction.correction: Use me apunto, me viene bien, or claro depending on intent
correction.tip: Me apunto means I'm in; me viene bien confirms timing.

quiz.meaning: In Spain, it means I have a cold.
quiz.example: No voy a salir; estoy constipado.

correction.mistake: Assuming actual, embarazada, and constipado mean their English lookalikes
correction.correction: Actual = current; embarazada = pregnant; constipado = having a cold in Spain
correction.example: La situación actual es distinta. — The current situation is different.
correction.tip: False friends look familiar—always learn them in a sentence.
